---
title: "Stage 5 — generate the eSAP"
---

Putting the chain into a study-level document, bound to the protocol's objectives, endpoints and
estimands.

## What this is

The eSAP is the container the chain goes into, and the input to execution. It is not a fourth
concept beside the other three — it is where a specification stops being about one endpoint and
starts being about a study.

It declares its own provenance, and the declaration is worth reading because it says what an
eSAP *is*: a join of three models — the study definition, the transformation model of the
previous two stages, and CDISC's Analysis Results Standard — naming which entities of each it
uses:

{{json:endpoints/01-simple-lab-cfb/esap.json#$provenance}}

## What you do

**The work:** assemble the completed chain into a study-level plan bound to the protocol's
objectives, endpoints and estimands — then read the estimand back before anything else, because
that is where an incomplete chain shows up.

1. Generate the plan from the study and the completed chain.
2. Read the estimand section first.

*In the application used here:* step 7, which renders the same state several ways — a sectioned
document, dataset and specification views, the JSON instance, and a Define-XML.

## What you should see

An eSAP whose estimand is populated: a named analysis population, named treatments, the
intercurrent event strategy, the summary measure. Not placeholders.

**On the two endpoints in this book you will see less than that, and it is not your mistake.**
Both estimands carry the population and both treatments. Both have an empty intercurrent-event
list, and both carry the population's name — `SAF` — in the summary-measure slot. The study
defines no estimand for either of its safety endpoints, which is ordinary; when nothing in the
study definition targets the endpoint, this application fills the summary from the chain's
population dimension and leaves the events empty, and nothing marks that it did. The eSAPs here
are left as emitted, so that what the tool does is on the record rather than tidied.

### Step into the factory

The generated plans are `endpoints/01-simple-lab-cfb/esap.json` and the two in
`endpoints/04-vitals-cfb-mmrm/`. The lesson below is item L6 in the lab endpoint's `log.md`,
with the two decisions it forced, D12 and D13; the fallback described above is item V2 in the
vitals endpoint's.

## What to look out for

**The estimand is assembled from two places, and the chain supplies half of it.** The
population-level summary and the intercurrent events come from the study definition; the
analysis population and the treatment come from the chain's own dimension values.

A chain that reaches this stage without those dimensions set produces an eSAP carrying
`AnalysisPopulation_unknown` and an unspecified intervention — structurally valid, semantically
empty. The study definition's own analysis-population reference is *not* what this step reads.

And when the study definition has no estimand for the endpoint at all, the half it was to
supply is not left blank: the summary-measure slot takes the chain's population name and the
event list is empty. Read the estimand knowing which of its fields came from where.

That is the same shape as the lesson in stage 2: there are two joins that look like one, and the
chain's is the one that carries. It is worth expecting the pattern rather than being surprised
by it twice.

*Check this on whatever tool you use: it is true of the application described here, at the
pinned commit, and is not a property of the concept model.*
